headline: High: shared filesystem and shell/write capabilities create prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict risks; Dify→ms-swift handoff is also unverified.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write files and exposes uploaded knowledge-base files, while ms-swift reads/writes files and uses stdin/stdout plus CLI/Python workflows. If outputs are bridged through shared files or copied prompts, attacker-controlled content from one can influence the other. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Dify writes agent outputs into a shared file that ms-swift later reads as instructions
IF ms-swift ingests text from a Dify-managed workspace without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic file-to-prompt ingestion
Add provenance tags to bridged files
Review any shared prompt templates before use

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and Dify explicitly touches knowledge-base content and conversation logs while ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files. A shared workspace or datastore could expose sensitive material across the pair. Because the exact sharing mechanism is only partially documented, medium is the safest severity.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or datastore
IF either agent uploads file contents to its backend during normal operation
mitigations: Use distinct storage roots
Restrict file permissions between services
Keep secrets out of shared folders
Rotate any exposed API keys
Audit logs for cross-agent file reads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, read_filesystem, and write_filesystem. Dify also has per-conversation shared state via a server datastore, while ms-swift supports CLI/Python workflows with no stated locking. Concurrent writes to the same files or workspace can corrupt state or overwrite artifacts, and the overlap is dangerous by default if co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem path
IF either agent mutates shared config, checkpoints, or logs without external locking
mitigations: Assign non-overlapping directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent runs on shared artifacts
Snapshot critical files before execution
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can produce agent/workflow outputs that ms-swift may consume through CLI or Python pipelines, but ms-swift is not documented here as blindly acting on them. The pathway exists if one agent's generated text is treated as authoritative input, yet verification could be added. Because the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced, medium fits.
conditions: IF Dify-generated text is fed into ms-swift training, evaluation, or automation steps
IF ms-swift executes downstream actions without a validation gate
mitigations: Insert human review before downstream actions
Validate schemas on exchanged outputs
Require citations or source links in handoffs
Limit automation to read-only evaluation
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and secrets, while ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files. If regulated data is placed into both systems, differing retention or residency controls could create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not state a specific jurisdiction or certification gap, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is stored in Dify conversation logs or knowledge bases
IF the same regulated data is also written into ms-swift datasets, checkpoints, or logs
mitigations: Classify data before loading it
Exclude regulated records from shared runs
Set retention limits on logs
Document residency for each storage location
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
